description: This case study is the IAEA report on off-site decontamination and remediation following the 11 March 2011 Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant accident, produced from a cooperation project between the IAEA and Fukushima Prefecture that ran from 2012 to 2022 under a Practical Arrangement signed in December 2012. The earthquake and tsunami and the resulting accident deposited radioactive contamination over parts of Japan, including Fukushima Prefecture, and the project complemented Japanese activities with assistance on radiation monitoring and remediation. The final version of September 2023 summarises the studies discussed in the project, reports experience gained in the prefecture in environmental monitoring of radionuclides and in studies of the behaviour of radiocaesium in the environment, and compares observations with studies elsewhere, highlighting similarities and differences between the Chernobyl and Fukushima Daiichi accidents. Access: PDF on the IAEA site, free; no licence text was found in the text read. Caveats: only the foreword was read closely, so the data matrix named in the file name and its contents are not verified. It suits recovery and remediation planning after nuclear accidents, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
